analysis.title: BorgWarner Inc. (BWA): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: BorgWarner's 3Q26 report was relatively solid versus tier 1 auto supplier peers that already reported (many of which lowered full year guidance), though more mixed on an absolute basis. Adjusted operating income, margin and EPS beat the Street (FactSet) while revenue was about in line.

BWA raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.20-$5.35 from $5.05-$5.30, citing share repurchases and a lower full-year tax rate. It kept its adjusted operating margin guidance at 10.7%-10.9% and cut the midpoint of revenue guidance, to $14.0-$14.2 bn from $14.0-$14.3 bn.

Implied 4Q26 guidance at the midpoint is below GS and the Street: revenue $3,432 mn vs GS $3,545 mn and Street $3,521 mn, adjusted operating margin 10.4% vs 10.9% (GS) and 11.0% (Street), and adjusted EPS $1.22 vs $1.31 for both GS and the Street.

Datacenter/energy initiatives are tracking to plan. The turbine generator system is still expected to reach start of production (SOP) in 2027 with more than $300 mn of 2027 sales, and external demonstrations are planned for 4Q.

The battery energy storage system product is being actively quoted and is expected to be ready for 2027 production. Bi-directional microgrid inverter samples have shipped to seven customers, quoting has begun with the first major customer, and SOP is still expected in 2027.

GS expects investor focus to be on whether revenue growth can accelerate beyond 2026 as prior-year automotive awards ramp and as the company expands into datacenter and energy markets. Margins and capital allocation are also expected to be call topics.

Segment detail: PowerDrive Systems revenue of $705 mn was 7.6% above GS and its EBIT margin of -0.7% was 180 bps better than GS. Battery & Charging Systems EBIT margin of -3.8% was 320 bps better than GS. Turbos & Thermal margin of 14.7% was 40 bps below GS, and Drivetrain & Morse revenue of $1,346 mn was 2.1% below GS.

The company cut gross debt by $864 mn in the quarter through a debt tender and make-whole redemption. It spent about $35 mn on dividends and $175 mn on share repurchases, and generated $195 mn of FCF. Full-year FCF guidance of $900 mn-$1,100 mn was maintained.

The company now expects CY26 weighted vehicle production markets down 2% to down 1% (from down 3% to about flat), with better Europe offset by weaker China and unchanged North America. Organic revenue growth guidance is now -4.0% to -2.5% from -3.5% to -1.5%.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps a Buy and $85 12-month target, based on 13x normalized EPS of $6.50. The stock closed at $55.93 on 28 Oct 2026, implying 52.0% upside.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue reported $3,487 mn (down 4% qoq, down 3% yoy organically) vs GS est $3,464 mn and Street (FactSet) est $3,497 mn.
3Q26 adjusted operating income reported $381 mn (10.9% margin) vs GS est $369 mn (10.7%) and Street est $372 mn (10.6%).
3Q26 operating EPS (non-GAAP) reported $1.39 vs GS est $1.23 and Street est $1.25, a beat of $0.16 and $0.14.
2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $5.20-$5.35 (midpoint $5.28) from $5.05-$5.30, vs GS est $5.20 and Street est $5.21. The raise is attributed to buybacks and a lower effective tax rate.
2026 revenue guidance is $14.0-$14.2 bn (midpoint $14.1 bn) vs GS and Street at about $14.2 bn. Adjusted operating margin guidance of 10.7%-10.9% is maintained vs GS and Street at 10.9%.
Implied 4Q26 guidance midpoint: revenue $3,432 mn, adjusted operating margin about 10.4%, adjusted EPS $1.22, vs GS est $3,545 mn / 10.9% / $1.31 and Street est $3,521 mn / 11.0% / $1.31.
GS 3Q26 EPS estimate was $1.23 for the quarter, and GS 2026E EPS is $5.20, 2027E $5.95 and 2028E $7.05.

risk_factors: Revenue growth and long-term profitability, including the effect of BorgWarner's exposure to EVs and of profits from ICE-related products.
A larger than anticipated tariff impact.
The overall growth of the automotive industry.
